title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 234 (Merger or amalgamation of company with foreign company)

content.overview: Section 234 provides for cross-border mergers: a foreign company may merge into a company registered under this Act (inbound), and a company registered under this Act may merge into a foreign company situated in a jurisdiction notified by the Central Government (outbound), subject to prior approval of the Reserve Bank of India and the conditions prescribed. The scheme otherwise follows the framework of sections 230 to 232. Only notified jurisdictions are eligible for an outbound merger. Valuation and creditor protection remain applicable.
content.glance: Cross-border merger: foreign → Indian (inbound) or Indian → foreign in notified jurisdiction (outbound); RBI prior approval; conditions prescribed; ss. 230–232 framework otherwise applies.
content.study: A foreign company may merge or amalgamate with a company registered under this Act, and a company registered under this Act may merge or amalgamate with a foreign company incorporated in a jurisdiction notified by the Central Government, with prior approval of the Reserve Bank of India and subject to such other conditions as may be prescribed. Current-law framing: identify inbound or outbound structure; for outbound, confirm the foreign jurisdiction is notified; obtain RBI prior approval; apply prescribed conditions; otherwise follow ss. 230–232 process (meetings, majority, Tribunal sanction, valuation and creditor protection). Distinct from purely domestic s. 232 mergers and from fast-track s. 233.

sections.heading: Inbound
sections.body: Foreign company may merge into a company registered under the Act.

sections.heading: Outbound
sections.body: Indian company may merge into a foreign company only if that foreign company is in a jurisdiction notified by the Central Government.

sections.heading: Approvals
sections.body: Prior approval of the Reserve Bank of India; other conditions as prescribed.

sections.heading: Process Overlay
sections.body: Scheme otherwise follows sections 230 to 232; valuation and creditor protection remain.

provisions.title: Merger or amalgamation of company with foreign company

examples.title: Inbound merger
examples.body: A foreign company merges into an Indian company under s. 234 with RBI prior approval. The scheme is processed under the ss. 230–232 framework with the additional cross-border conditions.

examples.title: Outbound only to notified jurisdictions
examples.body: An Indian company proposes to merge into a foreign company in a jurisdiction that has not been notified. Section 234 does not permit outbound merger into non-notified jurisdictions.

hypotheticals.question: Can an Indian company merge into any foreign company under s. 234 without more?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Outbound merger is limited to foreign companies in jurisdictions notified by the Central Government, and requires prior RBI approval and prescribed conditions. The domestic scheme process under ss. 230–232 still applies.

distinctions.title: Cross-border merger (s. 234) vs domestic merger (s. 232)
distinctions.left: Foreign company involved; RBI approval; outbound only to notified jurisdictions
distinctions.right: Domestic companies; Tribunal process under s. 232 without cross-border RBI/notification rules

misconceptions.trap: Any cross-border merger can proceed like a domestic s. 232 scheme without RBI involvement.
misconceptions.correction: Section 234 requires prior RBI approval and, for outbound mergers, a notified jurisdiction, in addition to the ss. 230–232 framework.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 234 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify inbound or outbound. II. For outbound, check notified jurisdiction. III. RBI approval and prescribed conditions. IV. Apply ss. 230–232 overlay. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Structure; jurisdiction; RBI status; scheme process; precise relief.

enhancement.definition: Section 234 permits merger of a foreign company into an Indian company, and of an Indian company into a foreign company in a notified jurisdiction, with prior RBI approval and prescribed conditions, otherwise under the ss. 230–232 framework.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Cross-border mergers are channelled through the domestic scheme process with additional exchange-control and jurisdictional gates.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 234 is the cross-border overlay on the merger chapter.
enhancement.problemApplication: Map direction; check jurisdiction and RBI; apply scheme process.
